GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-07-16T21:38:45Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Object Property List(of Object) - .contains not working
Description: Consider the below:

```
public class mRom
	public property Name as String
end class

public class mGames
	<BsonRef("mRoms")>
	public property AllRoms as List(of mRom)
end class

ugame = db.Collections.mGames.Include(Function(x) x.AllRoms).FindById(ssGameId)
If Not ugame.AllRoms.Contains(rom) Then ugame.AllRoms.Add(rom)
```

This is to review AllRoms and add `rom` to the list if an instance of `rom` isn't already in the list. HOwever, I get duplicate entries. 

The `.Contains` function never detects the presence of `rom`, even if it is already in the collection. 

What am I doing wrong?

REASONING: This issue is about a conceptual programming problem with the `.Contains()` method not working as expected on a List of objects. The problem is that the default implementation of `.Contains()` for reference types checks for reference equality, not value equality. When comparing custom objects like `mRom`, the method is looking for the exact same instance, not an object with the same property values. 

The solution would be to either:
1. Override the `Equals()` and `GetHashCode()` methods in the `mRom` class
2. Use LINQ with a custom comparison: `If Not ugame.AllRoms.Any(Function(x) x.Name = rom.Name) Then`
3. Implement `IEquatable<mRom>` interface

This is a common programming concept that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the code. The issue is about understanding how object equality works in .NET collections, which is a conceptual knowledge problem rather than something that requires execution to verify.
